digest.component_or_area: MCP server deployment and session lifecycle
propositions: Blue-green cutover swaps nginx /mcp upstream to new container while old container still holds active stateful MCP sessions, causing all in-flight client requests to receive 404 Session expired errors instead of routing to the session's original container.

MCP server is deployed in stateful session-managed mode by default (StreamableHTTPSessionManager) without explicit stateless_http configuration, making every session bound to a single container process and vulnerable to orphaning during redeploy.

Graceful drain via docker stop --time 1260 preserves the old container's lifetime but not its routing path, because nginx upstream is switched before clients can make requests to drain their sessions.
Clients receive opaque transport errors (rmcp::transport::worker) rather than actionable session-expired signals, preventing them from detecting the failure and reconnecting.
Switching to stateless_http mode is feasible (already available in FastMCP API) and eliminates session state affinity to containers, making blue-green cutover transparent to clients.
No rebar tool depends on server-initiated messages or session-scoped state, making stateless mode safe to implement without behavioral regression.
